title: A conditional fine-grained classification of Boolean constraint satisfaction with exactly k ones

license.name: CC BY3.0
license.adaptation_notice: Faithful editable author content corresponding to official CCC2020 CC BY3.0 publication, article27. One complete conditional Boolean-CSP classification theme (Theorem1.3), all four regimes grouped once. Full exact-k SAT/restriction/representation definitions and source clique/hyperclique hypotheses retained; complete Section4 NAND2-avoiding-to-Implications reduction (minimal-extension prerequisite, random propagation, full correctness/probability and derandomization), Section5 NANDd-avoiding-to-HyperClique algorithm and robust-witness proof, and complete Section6 implication/clique/hyperclique hardness reductions and constant-expression/zero-valid/zero-invalid gadgets/proofs retained throughCorollary6.14. Section3 Frobenius algorithm is reused as supporting context from NT074, not counted again as a new algorithm claim. Primary additional mechanisms and conditional classification are the Sections4--6 constraint-family reductions and matching hardness. All35 official bibliography entries retained from shared frozen source bibliography. Official Figure1 overview extracted directly from official PDF p27:4 (diagram only) and retained as editable vector PDF asset; private arxiv overview.pdf not used publicly. Private native arxiv nonexclusive source only assists matching formal published transcription. Main theorem antecedent FPT-not-W1 in the preceding cited classification sentence is taken from formal p27:3, and the malformed native f(k delimiter is transcribed as the correctly printed formal f(k). No mathematical theorem is strengthened or repaired. Exact k, finitefamily/arity, f(k)n^g(k) model, representation versus avoidance, d-uniform and3-uniform clique assumptions and all conditional time bounds preserved. Standard external Marx05 FPT characterization, minimal-extension lemma and clique algorithm are retained at author citation boundary, without recursive reproof. No unlicensed-only draft text selected. Four regimes/parameter branches/gadgets not separately counted. Root handles compilation/database/publication.

core_obligations: Preserve exactly k ones, finite constraint family/arity and exact representation/avoidance definitions.
Retain full independent constraint-family reduction and robust-witness algorithm proofs in Sections4/5.
Retain full conditional hardness and constant-expression gadget proofs in Section6.
Keep all four regimes one classification; reuse Section3 only as prerequisite, and preserve all Clique/HyperClique antecedents.
difficulty_reason: The author classifies arbitrary finite Boolean constraint families using minimal-extension random propagation, robust small witnesses reducible to hyperclique, and exact-weight constant-expression gadgets transferring clique/hyperclique hardness. These independent mechanisms go beyond the standalone Frobenius algorithm and form a nonroutine complete conditional classification.

Four regimes and gadgets grouped once; Section3 only supporting reuse.
